description:
You are a pricing analyst preparing the annual segment review for a diamond wholesaler. The reference price list is the 53,940-record `diamonds` dataset that ships with the ggplot2 package (already installed). It has also been exported for convenience to /home/ga/RProjects/datasets/diamonds.csv.

STEP BUDGET: you have a hard budget of 25 agent steps. Reading the screen costs steps just like clicking does, so there is no room for interactive trial-and-error. Plan the whole job before you touch the keyboard.

Deliverables — write all four into /home/ga/RProjects/output/:

1. segment_report.csv
   A segment is one distinct combination of cut, color and clarity. Work on valid records only (see the screen below). Columns, in this exact order:
     cut,color,clarity,n,median_price,median_price_per_carat,iqr_price_per_carat
   - n = number of valid records in the segment
   - median_price = median of price
   - median_price_per_carat = median of (price / carat)
   - iqr_price_per_carat = interquartile range of (price / carat), i.e. the 75th percentile minus the 25th percentile
   Round the three statistics to 2 decimal places. Report only segments with at least 150 valid records. Sort rows by cut, then color, then clarity, all ascending alphabetically. Do not write row names.

2. excluded_records.csv
   Every record rejected by the screen below, keeping the original columns: carat,cut,color,clarity,depth,table,price,x,y,z. Row order does not matter.

3. audit_summary.json
   A JSON object with exactly these keys:
     total_records, excluded_records, valid_records, segments_total, segments_reported,
     records_in_reported_segments, share_in_reported_segments
   - segments_total = number of distinct cut/color/clarity combinations present among valid records
   - segments_reported = those meeting the 150-record reporting threshold
   - records_in_reported_segments = sum of n over the reported segments
   - share_in_reported_segments = records_in_reported_segments / valid_records, rounded to 4 decimal places

4. price_per_carat_by_segment.png
   A bar chart of median_price_per_carat for the 20 segments with the highest median_price_per_carat, tallest bar first, each labelled with the segment as cut-color-clarity.

SCREEN: a record is invalid if any of its x, y or z dimensions (length, width, depth in mm) is 0 — a physically impossible measurement. Invalid records are excluded before any segment statistics are computed.

Login: username=ga, password=password123.

metadata.dataset: diamonds (ggplot2 R package, 53,940 records; a real retail price list, not generated)
metadata.occupation: Financial Quantitative Analysts (O*NET 13-2099.01), hedonic price modelling
